task.description: Sizing/diagnosis pass on ISS-0431 (no admission control / backpressure anywhere -- HTTP entry path primary surface, Poller secondary). Confirm the issue's own claim that no bounded-concurrency mechanism exists, review decision 0014's new-dependency policy for the library-vs-hand-rolled question, and make the WF-03 sizing call: scoped fix vs same-run CODE-DESIGNER design vs route to REQ-ANALYST for new requirement(s). Diagnosis only -- no fix implementation, no requirement drafting.

result.summary:
CONFIRMED BY DIRECT READ, not from the issue's prose alone: no bounded-concurrency/admission-control mechanism exists anywhere in lib/. `lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex` runs `Plug.Parsers` (body-size cap only, not a concurrency cap) then `assign_trace_id` -> `AuthPipeline` -> `TenantStatus` -> `match`/`dispatch` with no semaphore/queue/limiter plug in the chain at all; its own moduledoc table lists `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` as still 'deferred (S4, to port)' and unmounted, and rate limiting (per-client request-rate throttling) is in any case a different mechanism from admission control (bounding in-flight DB-connection-holding concurrency) -- porting RateLimit would not close this issue. `lib/letflow/application.ex` supervises Repo, five separate purpose-built `Task.Supervisor`s (SandboxPool, PluginTaskSupervisor, Lua.TaskSupervisor, two Wasm registries) and `Letflow.SandboxPool` itself, but none of them bound HTTP-request concurrency against the Ecto pool -- they bound unrelated subsystems (sandbox provisioning, plugin/script/wasm dispatch). `config/runtime.exs:113` sets `pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10")` with no accompanying admission cap referencing it anywhere. `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` (GenServer ticker, REQ-186) does an unbounded `Enum.each` over every tenant schema on every tick calling `Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1` -- no per-tenant or global concurrency limit, confirming the issue's 'Poller secondary surface' framing. `grep -rn 'semaphore\|admission\|rate_limit\|concurrency'` across `lib/` (excluding tests) surfaces only design-doc prose, the still-unmounted RateLimit plug, and unrelated per-row optimistic-concurrency patterns (Ecto unique-index races in repository.ex/tasks.ex) -- nothing that bounds simultaneous DB-connection-holding work. Issue's core claim fully confirmed: zero mechanism, either surface.

ZIG_VS_ELIXIR_FINDINGS.md: NOT REACHABLE in this working tree (`find / -iname 'ZIG_VS_ELIXIR_FINDINGS.md'` returned nothing from the repo root outward within this session's search scope). Stating this explicitly per this project's convention for unreachable R-Co-adjacent material, rather than fabricating Race 3's content -- its claims are taken as reported verbatim in ISS-0431.yaml's own description (200-connection exhaustion of Postgres max_connections=100, Zig-side fix an atomic-CAS semaphore capping concurrency at 40, Elixir side explicitly never stress-tested for the equivalent) and not independently re-verified here.

Four prior LOCAL mitigations read in full (docs/issues/ISS-0194, ISS-0219, ISS-0222, ISS-0224, all resolved): each is a DIFFERENT ad hoc shape solving the identical root cause (unbounded demand vs. a bounded connection resource) with no shared mechanism -- ISS-0194 computed a derived `TEST_POOL_SIZE` to cap demand against `max_connections`; ISS-0219 was resolved via documentation/guidance on `TEST_PARALLEL_N`, not a code cap; ISS-0222 is an undiagnosed transient launch-timing spike with only a settling-gap recommendation, no cap at all; ISS-0224 (an admission-control-shaped defect inside `Letflow.SandboxPool` itself -- synchronous `provision_sandbox/0` blocking the pool mailbox so `max_wait_ms` isn't honoured under concurrent claims) was explicitly SCOPED OUT of its own parent fix (ISS-0220) specifically because a real fix means moving provisioning into a monitored `Task` with slot bookkeeping across an async completion -- i.e. even SandboxPool's own local admission/wait-queue logic was deferred as non-trivial, and it still has no shared mechanism with the other three. A real ISS-0431 fix that invents a fifth ad hoc local variant (e.g. a bare `pool_size`-only fix scoped to just the HTTP plug chain, ignoring Poller and the SandboxPool precedent) would repeat exactly the pattern the issue exists to end.

Decision 0014 (new-dependency policy, read in full): not literally about admission-control libraries, but its reasoning transfers directly to the 'library vs. hand-rolled semaphore' open question ISS-0431 names. 0014's method for a build-vs-bind choice is: identify the real hazard class for THIS use case, check whether a pure-BEAM option removes it outright vs. merely mitigating it, and treat a new native/NIF dependency as a real, disclosed cost requiring REVIEWER sign-off on the first PR introducing it (0014's Decision point (f): 'wasmex... introduces Letflow's first native-code build dependency... CI must gain a Rust toolchain'). For admission control specifically: the workload is bounding concurrent BEAM-process/GenServer-mediated access to Ecto connections -- a problem the BEAM's own primitives (a GenServer-backed counting semaphore, `:queue` + monitors, or `Task` supervision patterns already used five times over in application.ex) solve natively with no native/NIF surface at all, so 0014's crash-isolation argument for Lua ('removes the hazard class entirely rather than mitigating it... killable by ordinary BEAM means') argues for a hand-rolled or pure-BEAM-library semaphore here too, not a NIF-backed one. Whether an existing pure-BEAM hex package (e.g. a counting-semaphore or a bounded-queue library) or a small hand-rolled GenServer is preferred is exactly the kind of narrow implementation choice 0014 itself treats as REQUIRING its own comparison once a requirement is scoped -- not resolvable here without first fixing the harder, genuinely-open product questions below.

SIZING VERDICT, using ISS-0411's own diagnosis criteria (new architectural decision with no existing pattern to extend + multi-file/multi-surface scope + a decision-record-adjacent tradeoff => route through REQ-ANALYST rather than fix as a scoped WF-03 issue or design in a same-run CODE-DESIGNER pass): THIS IS NOT A SCOPED WF-03 FIX, and it does not fit a single same-run CODE-DESIGNER pass either. Three reasons, matching ISS-0411's bar: (1) the issue's own 'TO DECIDE, not prescribed' list is not one design choice but at least three coupled, genuinely open PRODUCT/architecture decisions that a design doc cannot make unilaterally without becoming a de facto requirement -- response shape (503+Retry-After vs. another shape, an HTTP-contract change every API client must handle), and especially global-vs-per-tenant-vs-both caps, which the issue itself flags as 'arguably the more important property in a multi-tenant BPM platform' and which is a multi-tenancy fairness/SLA decision, not an implementation detail; (2) it spans two independent supervision-tree surfaces (`Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`/Bandit request path, and `Letflow.Scheduler.Poller`'s per-tick tenant sweep) that the issue explicitly says must be covered 'by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap, as has now happened four times' -- i.e. the deliverable is required BY THE ISSUE ITSELF to be a single coherent cross-cutting mechanism, which is requirement-sized scope, not a single-module patch; (3) it has direct implications for decision-record-adjacent policy (0014's native-dependency cost/REVIEWER-sign-off precedent applies if a library is chosen) and for `config/runtime.exs`'s `pool_size`/`POOL_SIZE` and Postgres `max_connections` so the three don't drift a fifth time -- an operational/config contract spanning stages, which REQ-ANALYST-level acceptance criteria are the right place to pin down (e.g. 'the admission cap MUST be expressible as a function of pool_size, verified by test, not a second independently-tuned number'), not something a single design doc can silently assert without its own validating requirement.

RECOMMENDATION TO ORCH (mirroring ISS-0411's own routing, which recommended REQ-ANALYST-drafted requirement(s) rather than dispatching REQ-ANALYST directly): dispatch REQ-ANALYST to draft one or more properly-sized S6 requirements covering (a) a per-tenant admission cap on the HTTP entry path (the issue's own stated priority surface and its own stated 'more important' fairness property), (b) a global cap or ceiling composing with (a) rather than replacing it, (c) extending the same mechanism to Poller's per-tenant sweep loop as a secondary requirement or as an explicit AC of the same requirement, and (d) an explicit, testable relationship between the chosen cap(s) and `pool_size`/`POOL_SIZE`/Postgres `max_connections` so ISS-0194/0219/0222/0224's drift pattern cannot recur a fifth time. REQ-ANALYST's draft should treat 0014's reasoning (pure-BEAM primitive preferred over a NIF-backed one; any new hex dependency choice needs its own brief comparison) as a steering precedent, and should note the SandboxPool precedent (ISS-0224) as prior art for the wait-queue/backpressure shape worth reusing or explicitly deviating from. Response-shape (503+Retry-After) should be pinned as an explicit acceptance criterion of whichever requirement covers the HTTP surface, not left to CODE-DESIGNER to invent later. This record (ISS-0431) should stay open pending that requirement's completion, per ISS-0411's own precedent for not closing an issue whose real fix has only been diagnosed, not delivered.
